Figure 1:A controlled routing pair replaces a large sampler-noise
group.Sampler-space GRPO injects continuous noise into the reverse process
and estimates an advantage from many complete visual rollouts. RPO retains
the original deterministic sampler and pairs two rollouts that share the
prompt, initial visual latent, routed denoising levels, and anchor layers.
They differ only in their sampled attention routes, so their reward difference
measures the aggregate effect of the two recorded routed trajectories.
Generated visual outputs are schematic.

Figure 2:A temporary route perturbs training rollouts, and a velocity
likelihood updates the dense generator.At each routed leveltt, the
native attention mass of every query block over the key blocks defines a
categorical draw over the candidate blocksCqC_{q}and a dense option, while
the safety blockSqS_{q}stays active. Two matched rollouts record independent
routes under the same prompt, content seed, routed levels, and anchor layers.
Replay recomputes the dense velocity at every recorded routed latent, and the
reward difference weights a Gaussian likelihood of the routed step around it.
At inference, RPO removes all masks and runs dense attention with the
original deterministic sampler.

Figure 3:RPO on Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium.(a) Samples before and after RPO on DrawBench prompts. Each pair shares the
prompt and initial noise. (b, c) DrawBench scores over1,0001{,}000images from200200prompts with55seeds, generated without classifier-free guidance.
RPO improves desired property across all five reported metrics.

Figure 5:Text-to-video samples from Wan2.2-TI2V-5B before and after
RPO.Each row shows one prompt. For each model we show the first and last of
the 13 generated frames (1280×7041280\times 704, 50 sampling steps). Both models
use the same prompt and initial noise. RPO follows the prompt more closely and
replaces distorted, painterly textures with coherent, realistic scenes.
